exposure: Maternal meal frequency patterns (snack meal, main meal, evening meal)
cohort: The study included 66,000 pregnant women from the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study (MoBa).
finding: Regular consumption of main meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) during mid-pregnancy was associated with a lower risk of preterm delivery, particularly in women with BMI <25 kg/m2.
gest_age: Preterm delivery was defined as birth at <37 gestational weeks.
